sources_checked: GitHub code search for replay/world model/averaging/consolidation terms

assessment.reason: O's Context Kernel already treats context as having overload/interference cost and records selected/excluded context; O also has deterministic cross-family retention tests. The new contribution is external theoretical/empirical evidence that replay quantity is non-monotonic and random replay can be harmful, not the generic idea that more context can interfere.

O has acquisition-order retention tests, but the inspected code checks whether order causes forgetting; it does not implement a prototypical-first then progressively harder retrieval/rehearsal scheduler or measure equal-retention cost reduction.

Repository search found no world-model implementation. The candidate is not generic memory retention: it separates reward/task adaptation from continually learned dynamics and moves task solving into planning.

No direct checkpoint/model-averaging continual-learning implementation was found in the targeted search. O contains replay and retention machinery, so a broader semantic comparison is still needed before promotion.

next_queries: Quantify Online Agent/ContinualBench margins versus specific deep world-model baselines and identify ablations for shallow FTL model versus MPC/planning.
Find direct LLM/agent evidence for compatibility-aware memory retrieval or easy-to-hard rehearsal ordering.
Search O for semantic equivalents of checkpoint averaging beyond literal keyword matches before sending SFA as a novel candidate.
Find active-learning/curriculum mechanisms with measured reduction in total updates or wall-clock at fixed retention/transfer quality.

continuation.frontier: External evidence is now being filtered against O's actual implementation. Prioritize mechanisms with genuine context asymmetry: world-model/task separation and replay-order scheduling; treat harmful-replay/confounder results mainly as calibration of O's existing context-interference/evaluation principles.
